xep.header:
User Applications This specification defines an XMPP protocol extension for communicating information about the applications or games that a user may be running. &LEGALNOTICE; xxxx ProtoXEP Standards Track Standards Council
XMPP Core XMPP IM XEP-0060 XEP-0163
NOT_YET_ASSIGNED
Sigrid Einarsson techmetx11@disroot.org techmetx11@disroot.org
0.0.1 2026-06-19 techmetx11
First draft.

section1.p: &xep0060; and &xep0163; can be used to publish a wide variety of "extended presence" information about users. This XEP specifies an extended presence payload format that communicates information about the games a user plays or applications a user is using. This information may be of interest to a user's contacts and can also be used in social networking applications.

Though, the previous XEP related, which was &xep0196; did not succeed in achieving this goal. This XEP also intends to be a base for compatibility with other non-standard rich presence implementations (Discord Rich Presence/RPC, etc.) that applications may be using to broadcast information about themselves.

section2.p: Information about applications are provided by and are propagated on the network by the user's client. The information container for application data is a <app/> element that is qualified by the 'urn:xmpp:user_app:0' namespace. The application information itself is provided as the XML character data of the following children of the <app/> element:

tr.td: What the user is currently doing in the application.

section2.p: NOTE: The datatypes specified above are defined in &w3xmlschema2;.
Additional information about the presence can be provided in a child element with its own XML namespace.

When a user starts playing a game or running an application, its client may publish that fact to PEP node whose NodeID is "urn:xmpp:user_app:0" &NSNOTE; or to a generic pubsub node. Because application information is not pure presence information and can change independently of the user's availability, it SHOULD NOT be provided as an extension to the &PRESENCE; stanza type.

There SHOULD be an attribute within <app/> named "from", that describes where the presence info was sourced from. If this is not present, then it is assumed that the presence information is provided by the user themselves.
The application information is then delivered to all subscribers:

example.caption: Application Information is Delivered to All Subscribers

section2.p: When the user stops playing the game or using the applicatoin, the user's client SHOULD send an empty <app/> element with the same ItemID:

example.caption: Stop Information is Delivered to All Subscribers

section1.p: The programs/games that a user runs may be sensitive. A client MUST provide a way for a user to configure which programs or types of programs will not be published (e.g., via user preferences).
This document requires no interaction with &IANA;.
